question: Which canonical mappings preserve document meaning through Markdown parse/serialize, and where must loss be explicit?
trigger: Explicit harsh final review of a critique that challenged the prior Markdown audit for preserving MDX as the official default dialect.
requirements: Ordinary CommonMark, GFM and math input must not fail or change meaning because Plate extension syntax is installed.
Plate-specific extension elements must remain feature-owned, structurally composable, diagnosable and serializable without making full MDX the default language.
Expected source and schema refusals return results rather than escaping as runtime exceptions; source locations remain meaningful.
Do not delete compatibility machinery until its replacement proves current HTML-like extension inputs, legacy reads and streaming prefixes.
Separate generic loss accounting from property preservation, and retain persisted-ID writing only for a named current consumer.
Assessment and review-history repair only; no product implementation or downstream plan.
evidenceReuse: Reused the source-matching public/helper census and focused parser/serializer observations from the two 2026-09-28 Markdown audits. Rechecked the official registry kit, package primitive, parser and AI final-preview path; ran focused default-kit/CommonMark probes for angle-bracket text, autolinks, braces, indented code, comments, inline block tags, void HTML, serializer dependence and attribute coercion. Two bounded independent reviews separately validated behavior and compared full MDX, CommonMark HTML pairing, JSX-only and selective micromark directions.
summary: Pursue the Markdown redesign but supersede the prior target. The package primitive is neutral; the official registry kit selects full MDX as ordinary Markdown, causing valid CommonMark to fail or silently change and causing completed AI output to disappear. Make CommonMark + GFM + math the official default and MDX explicit. Before choosing the extension parser, prototype a bounded registered-tag pass over CommonMark HTML nodes against a selective micromark extension. Normalize either into a neutral feature-owned extension node. Keep htmlToJsx and recovery until that replacement wins, then remove the MDX-specific workaround chain. Reopen withBlockId writing absent a current consumer, split generic property accounting from preservation, and move attribute decoding to schema owners.

reconciliation.question: Which canonical mappings preserve document meaning through Markdown parse/serialize, and where must loss be explicit?
reconciliation.reason: Retains its API census, unearned-surface cuts, feature ownership, exact typing, references, mark/list repairs and diagnostics, but replaces its MDX-preserving target and unsafe htmlToJsx deletion order. It also reopens the unearned persisted-ID writer and separates property accounting from preservation.

alternatives: Keep full MDX in the official kit and repair recovery: Stop; ordinary CommonMark remains subordinate to a stricter language, preserving the root cause and AI final-output failure.
Delete htmlToJsx while retaining full MDX: Stop; raw remark-mdx rejects currently accepted void HTML and table line breaks, so this sequencing is a regression.
Use the upstream MDX JSX-only extension: Stop as the default; it still claims angle-bracket syntax and rejects ordinary generic-looking text and autolinks.
Use a bounded registered-tag pass over CommonMark HTML nodes: Pursue as the leading prototype; it preserves the standard grammar if it can pair locally without becoming a general HTML parser.
Build a selective micromark extension for registered Plate tags: Retain as the fallback prototype; it offers parser-native structure at materially higher ownership cost.
Keep full MDX as an explicit dialect adapter over neutral extension nodes: Pursue; real MDX sources have a separate job and should not define ordinary Markdown.
Keep withBlockId writing because Markdown crosses a serialized boundary: Stop absent a named current consumer; preserve compatible reads and only retain writing if a real persistence job pays for it.
proofLimits: Read-only product audit; only review artifacts and ledger metadata changed. Focused probes reproduce the official-kit failures and unsafe cut ordering, but no checked-in executable probe or official CommonMark corpus run was added. CommonMark raw HTML observations prove that extension structure is not free; they do not select the final pairer, tag syntax, malformed-tag policy, compatibility cost or streaming performance. No product implementation, full package/type suite, browser/native clipboard, external viewer or benchmark ran.
